answer: Each new identity must post a small refundable bond, then build a thread of linked attestations: a series of tiny, time-staggered tasks, each verified by a different established peer, so one identity's history cannot be copied onto another. Like light through a prism, a single reputation is split and checked from many independent angles, and any mismatch breaks the thread. A sparrow-sized flock of fake identities would still have to pay a bond and perform real verified work per identity, so mass forgery costs more than it can ever earn.
